tool.name: MovebankAnimalTracks

summary.para:
View online help files: https://www.jennessent.com/data-tools/movebank-animal-tracks.html
Loads an animal tracking dataset published in the Movebank Data Repository as points (one for every location fix), as track lines (one for every animal, through its fixes in order of time), or both. The dataset is named by its DOI. Its files are fetched without an account and kept on disk, and its license and citation are recorded with the output. A study in Movebank itself can be loaded as well, named by its study ID: that needs your own Movebank sign-in, the owner's permission to download, and your acceptance of the study's license terms. A dataset already on disk can be loaded again from its folder. This is the scripting form of the Movebank Animal Tracks window on the ribbon, which searches the repository and Movebank and then runs this tool, so that every run of the window is recorded in the Geoprocessing History. Works at every license level.

tool.usage:
What the Movebank Data Repository is. Movebank (movebank.org) is a database of animal tracking data, organized by study. Most studies in it are private to their owners. The Movebank Data Repository (datarepository.movebank.org) holds the datasets that owners have chosen to publish: each has a DOI, a license and a citation, and its files can be fetched without a Movebank account. This tool loads those published datasets, and, with a Movebank sign-in, the studies in Movebank that your account may download.
A small fraction of Movebank. Most of the data on Movebank can be reached only with a Movebank account and the permission of the person who posted them. The published datasets, which need neither, are a small fraction of what Movebank holds. So the odds are slim that you will find the species you want to study in the area you are interested in. The published datasets are good for seeing how a species moves in general: they suit conceptual questions about animal movement better than an analysis of a particular species in a particular place.
Studies in Movebank, with your own account. A signed-in Movebank account may download the studies whose owners allow it, which are many more than have been published. Name a study by its Movebank study ID, as study 433126. The sign-in is your own Movebank user name and password, kept on your computer in Windows Credential Manager under the name JennessWildlifeTools.Movebank; sign in from the Movebank Animal Tracks window, or store it from a Command Prompt with cmdkey /generic:JennessWildlifeTools.Movebank /user:YOUR_MOVEBANK_USERNAME /pass. It is sent only to www.movebank.org, over an encrypted connection, and is never written to a message, a file or the metadata. A study is not a published dataset: it has no DOI, and its owner can add to it and correct it, so the same request made later may return different data. Movebank strongly encourages users to contact a study's owner about the intended use of its data, and to offer co-authorship or other credit as appropriate.
License terms of a study. Movebank hands over a study only after your account has accepted the study's license terms. When they have not been accepted, the tool stops, fetches nothing, and shows the terms in its messages. Read them. If you accept them, check I have read and accept the study's license terms and run the tool again: the tool then accepts them in the name of your account and fetches the data. Movebank remembers the acceptance, and does not ask again unless the owner changes the terms. The terms are written into a README beside the data and into the output's metadata, under Use Limitations.
No search by area. The Movebank Data Repository offers no way to find tracks by where they are. A published dataset's record holds its species, animals, number of locations, license and citation, but no coordinates, and Movebank's own service can limit fixes only by animal, date and sensor. So a published dataset cannot be chosen by study area, and its tracks are seen only once it is loaded. Judge where a dataset is from its title, keywords and summary. A study in Movebank has one main location, set by its owner, and the window can list the studies whose main location is in a study area.
The window or the tool. The Movebank Animal Tracks window (Data Tools group, Online Data) searches the repository by species, common name or keyword and shows each dataset's animals, locations, license and citation. Its last step runs this tool. To automate a request, make it once in the window, then right-click its entry in the Geoprocessing History and choose Copy Python Command.
Naming the dataset. Give the dataset's DOI, with or without doi: or https://doi.org/ in front (for example 10.5441/001/1.74pf3n2p), or its address in the repository. Or give a Movebank study, as study 433126 (see above). Or give a folder, or a single data file, that already holds a dataset in Movebank's CSV format; nothing is fetched then.
The files. A published dataset usually holds one or more data files, a reference-data file that describes the animals, tags and deployments, and a README. The tool fetches those into a folder named after the output, inside Data_Downloads in the project folder (beside the output geodatabase when the tool runs outside a project), and keeps them. A file that is already there at its full size is not fetched again. Read the README: it describes the study and the terms its owner sets.
Points. One point for every location fix, in WGS 84. The fields are the columns of Movebank's data file with hyphens and colons written as underscores (individual-local-identifier becomes individual_local_identifier). The time of the fix is written twice: as a date field, and as text exactly as the file gives it, in UTC. Each of the dataset's other columns becomes a whole-number field or a decimal-number field only when every value in it is one, and a text field otherwise, so nothing is lost; a column with no values is left out. Rows that are measurements without a location, such as accelerometer readings, are not loaded.
Track lines. One line for every animal, through its fixes in order of time, with the number of fixes, the first and last times, the duration in days, the length in kilometers (geodesic), and the animal's sex and life stage where the reference data give them. A line shows the order of the fixes, not the path the animal took between them, so its length is the least distance the animal travelled. A line that crosses the 180th meridian is cut there, so it does not run the long way around the map.
Outliers. Data owners mark fixes they judge to be wrong by setting the fix's visible attribute to false. Those fixes are left out unless you ask for them.
License and citation. Each dataset carries its own license, and its owner asks to be cited. The messages give the license, the citation and the DOI of any related publication, and the output's metadata records them. The metadata also holds the dataset's README: the whole of it under Description, and its terms of use under Use Limitations. All use of Movebank data is also subject to Movebank's general terms of use.

param.name: dataset
param.displayname: Dataset (the DOI of a dataset in the Movebank Data Repository, a Movebank study such as study 433126, or a folder or data file already on disk)

dialogReference.para: The DOI of a published dataset, such as 10.5441/001/1.74pf3n2p (with or without doi: or https://doi.org/ in front), or its address in the Movebank Data Repository. Or a study in Movebank itself, written as study and its Movebank study ID (study 433126), which is read with your own Movebank sign-in and needs the owner's permission to download and your acceptance of its license terms. Or the path of a folder, or of one data file, that already holds a dataset in Movebank's CSV format; nothing is fetched then, and the output carries no DOI or citation.

bulletList.bullet_item: Points and track lines: both feature classes.
Points: one point for every location fix, with all of the dataset's attributes.
Track lines: one line for every animal, through its fixes in order of time.

dialogReference.para: The point feature class to create, directly inside a file geodatabase (not in a feature dataset). Movebank's field names are too long for a shapefile.

param.name: out_lines
param.displayname: Output track lines (in a file geodatabase)

dialogReference.para: The line feature class to create, directly inside a file geodatabase (not in a feature dataset).

param.name: animals
param.displayname: Only these animals (their identifiers, separated by semicolons; empty for all)

dialogReference.para: The identifiers of the animals to load, exactly as the dataset writes them (its individual-local-identifier values), separated by semicolons. If a name is not in the dataset, the tool stops and lists the names that are.
Leave out fixes before this date and time (UTC). Empty for no limit.
Leave out fixes after this date and time (UTC). A date with no time of day covers that whole day. Empty for no limit.

param.name: include_flagged
param.displayname: Include fixes the data owner flagged as outliers

dialogReference.para: Unchecked, fixes whose visible attribute is false are left out, which is what the data owner intends. Checked, they are included; their visible field is false.

param.name: accept_terms
param.displayname: I have read and accept the study's license terms (a Movebank study only)

dialogReference.para: Used only when the dataset is a study in Movebank. Movebank hands over a study only after your account has accepted the study's license terms.
Unchecked, a study whose terms your account has not yet accepted is not fetched: the tool stops and shows the terms in its messages, so that you can read them.

Checked, the tool accepts the terms in the name of your Movebank account and then fetches the data. Check it only after you have read the terms and accept them. Movebank remembers the acceptance and does not ask again unless the owner changes the terms, so the box has no effect on a study whose terms are already accepted.
The DOI of the dataset that was loaded; empty for files on disk.

param.name: download_folder
param.displayname: Folder of the dataset's original files

dialogReference.para: The folder that holds the dataset's data files, reference data and README.

scriptExample.title: Movebank Animal Tracks example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Load a published pronghorn dataset as points and as one track line per animal.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.jenness.MovebankAnimalTracks( dataset="10.5441/001/1.74pf3n2p", output="Points and track lines", out_points=r"D:\data\tracks.gdb\Pronghorn_points", out_lines=r"D:\data\tracks.gdb\Pronghorn_tracks")

scriptExample.title: One summer, track lines only
scriptExample.para: The same dataset, limited to the fixes of June through August 2018.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.jenness.MovebankAnimalTracks( dataset="10.5441/001/1.74pf3n2p", output="Track lines", out_lines=r"D:\data\tracks.gdb\Pronghorn_summer_2018", date_from="2018-06-01", date_to="2018-08-31")

scriptExample.title: A study in Movebank, with your own account
scriptExample.para: A study named by its Movebank study ID. The sign-in is read from Windows Credential Manager. Run it first without accept_terms to read the study's license terms in the messages; add accept_terms=True only if you accept them.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.jenness.MovebankAnimalTracks( dataset="study 433126", output="Points and track lines", out_points=r"D:\data\tracks.gdb\Bats_points", out_lines=r"D:\data\tracks.gdb\Bats_tracks", accept_terms=True)
